newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU-based U.S. companies fear Cuba row fallout.
newsitem.headline: EU-based U.S. companies fear Cuba row fallout.

text.p: European companies of U.S. parentage warned on Monday that growing trade tension on Cuba policy between the European Union and Washington risked causing lasting damage to transatlantic business ties.
"The potential for lasting damage is serious," William Seddon-Brown, chairman of the EU committee of the American Chamber of Commerce in Beligum, said in a news statement.

"Unilateral sanctions which seek to address perceived wrongs committed outside U.S. territory, and the counter-measures which they provoke from the EU and other countries, are in conflict with shared policy values (and) damage economic relations between transatlantic partners...," the statement said.
The sanctions reference was to Washington's Helms-Burton Act on Cuba and retaliatory measures under consideration by the 15 countries of the European Union.

Transatlantic relations have soured in the wake of Helms-Burton, which includes provisions for naturalised Americans to take action in U.S. courts against "traffickers" -- foreign companies or individuals accused of gaining from investments made in property confiscated in Cuba since the 1959 Communist revolution.
The European Union, whose companies and citizens would be among those hit by the act, condemned the United States for enacting laws which apply outside its borders.
The bloc's complaints are due for an airing on November 20 before a World Trade Organisation panel, as are their gripes on similar U.S. laws seeking to quash trade with Iran and Libya.

European Union foreign ministers are due on Monday to vote on proposals that would allow countersuits to be brought anywhere in Europe against litigants who sue European companies or individuals for contravening the Helms-Burton Act.
